transcript.text: Hi everyone. The public API rate-limit project is up for its production policy review on August 25, and I'll be making the final call on what we communicate to customers. Before I record the policy, I need to hear from each of you — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — on any release-impacting findings you have. The current draft allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and doesn't specify a staffed launch window. Let's go through your findings so I can finalize this.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a backend finding before we proceed. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this directly impacts the policy we're about to finalize.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a customer success finding to share. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered this clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this directly impacts our rollout timing for at least one major customer.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a security finding to share. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it directly impacts the policy we're about to finalize — the current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which is too high given what I observed.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a support operations finding to share. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this directly impacts the launch window for the policy we're about to finalize.

Set a separate authentication endpoint limit of 30 requests per minute per API key in the final policy.
Send Acme their API limit notice on September 1 so enforcement is permitted on September 15 per their contract.
